metadata.title: Who are Europe’s startup alternatives to Palantir?

content.text:
Europe's desire for tech sovereignty is giving homegrown startups a chance at contracts held by US suppliers, and Palantir is a key target for disruption.
On Wednesday (Nov. 11), German drone maker Helsing unveiled Clarity, an agentic intelligence platform for the military. The $18 billion startup said that the platform is built around customised AI agents trained on military data to help armed forces to process data, identify threats and counter them. The system is a competitor to Palantir's Maven Smart System and is set to be trialled with Germany's military, the Financial Times reported.
Europe's governments have become more vocal this year about concerns over their reliance on Palantir's technology. The US tech giant supplies data and analytics across the military and police, as well as public sector agencies such as health and customs. In the private sector, its clients range from BMW to Axel Springer.
Its presence in Europe, however, has sparked backlash. The company's contract with the National Health Service in the UK has come under fierce scrutiny, especially since reports emerged last week that it would be extended. Over 120 organisations and unions across Europe issued a joint call in September to scrap all public sector contracts with Palantir.
It seems that Europe is taking note. In April, Germany's digital minister Karsten Wildberger told Politico that Europe needs a domestic alternative, while in June, members of Parliament in the UK warned that Palantir's presence in the public sector is an "unacceptable point of weakness". The same month, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced that the country's domestic intelligence agency, DGSI, would phase out Palantir's software, although Palantir said that its contract remains in force.
As the tide turns against Palantir, opportunities are opening up for local startups. Below is a list of companies offering alternatives that could see more demand as Europe's push for sovereignty gathers pace.
This article originally appeared on PitchBook News
